text:
The emergency lights died an hour ago. Now the lab breathes in the pale blue afterglow of failing backup batteries, and every shadow looks like it's waiting for you. You move quickly and quietly—old habits from security drills nobody ever thought you'd actually need. Two bottles of water. Two sandwiches, already stale. A flashlight, a lighter, a length of rope you grabbed without quite knowing why. No medkit—those went to people who needed them more, weeks ago, and never came back. No weapon, either. You were supposed to save the world with equations, not your hands.

The Scutum blueprints are rolled tight against your spine, wrapped in a torn garbage bag against the ash that gets into everything now. Three years of your life folded into a few hundred pages. Maybe humanity's last real chance, if even half of what you calculated holds true. You still believe that. You have to. But the blueprints alone are worthless without the Key, and the Key is locked inside HQ, on the far edge of a city that stopped being safe long before the Fracture finished the job.

You take one last look at the only home you've had since everything fell apart, and you don't let yourself wonder whether you'll ever stand in it again.

The battery is still humming faintly when you find it—a small miracle, fully charged, sitting on a shelf like it's been waiting for you specifically. Li-ion, rare, the kind of thing that could buy safe passage from someone desperate enough to want it, or power something that actually matters when the time comes. You do the math without meaning to: it's heavy, your pack is already full, and the only room left is where a bottle of water or a sandwich used to be. Somewhere out there, your body will remember this decision long after you've forgotten making it. You linger at the lab's threshold a moment longer than you should, then step out into a corridor gone unfamiliar with dust.

choices.text: Take the battery, leave a bottle of water.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You stow the battery and give up precious water. It could be worth the risk.

choices.text: Take the battery, leave a sandwich.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You tuck the battery in your bag and leave behind a meal.

choices.text: Leave the battery, keep all your supplies.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You can't risk losing water or food. You leave the battery behind.

text: The pharmacy sign has lost half its letters, but the shape of the word is still there if you squint—PHARMACY, or what's left of it, hanging crooked over a door someone thought to chain shut before the world ended. Smart of them. Frustrating for you. The chain is rusted but solid, looped through a padlock that's seen better decades. Somewhere behind that door is exactly what your body has been quietly begging for since you left the lab—bandages, maybe something for the headache building behind your eyes. You could work the lock slow and careful, praying nobody's watching. Or you could just end it—one hard strike, and deal with whoever comes running.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You take your time and manage to pick the lock, slipping inside unnoticed. While you were trying to pick the lock, you cut your first finger.
You break the lock, but the sound echoes into the street. Supplies are within reach, but you may have drawn attention.
You decide it's not worth the risk and move on, empty-handed.

text: Dust hangs thick in the air inside, backlit by a shaft of grey daylight through a cracked skylight. The shelves have mostly been picked clean by people who got here first, but you find a handful of bandages tucked behind a fallen display, and a bottle of painkillers three years past their expiration date—close enough, you decide, when the alternative is nothing at all. You allow yourself a moment. Just one. You sit against the counter, eat, drink, let your hands stop shaking. It's the closest thing to peace you've felt since the lights went out. Then you're moving again, because peace is not a thing you get to keep.

choices.text: Leave some supplies for another survivor.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You take what you need and leave the rest for someone else. It's a small kindness.

text: The noise brought them, exactly like you feared it would. Three of them, maybe four, filling the doorway before you've even had time to feel good about what you found. Their eyes go straight to your pack, and you understand immediately that this isn't a negotiation so much as a formality before the taking. One of them has a length of pipe held loose at his side, not quite threatening yet, but close. Your mind races through what you're carrying and what you can afford to lose, and how much of it is actually a choice.

ifTrue.narrativeOutcome: You hand over the battery. The scavengers let you go with most of your supplies.

ifFalse.narrativeOutcome: You forgot that you left the battery at the lab. The scavengers become hostile and violent, taking everything except one bottle of water.

choices.text: Try to talk your way out.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You plead with the scavengers. They take some of your supplies but let you leave unharmed.
You sprint out the back. You escape, but you drop some supplies and are left shaken. At least you've managed to grab one medkit.

text: You put the pharmacy behind you and don't look back—looking back never changed anything, in your experience, except how fast your heart beats. The street ahead is empty, or empty enough. Hunger sits low and constant in your stomach, an old companion by now. You're alive. For the moment, that has to be enough.

Night comes down over the city like something falling, not something arriving. You find an alley narrow enough that nobody could approach without you hearing, and you risk a small fire—just enough to keep the worst of the cold at bay, cupped low behind a wall of broken crates so the light won't carry. It feels obscenely good, the warmth, more than it should. Somewhere out in the dark, voices rise and fall. A dog barks, then another. Once, briefly, something that might have been a scream. You build a nest of cardboard and stolen blankets and tell yourself you'll only close your eyes for a minute.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You close your eyes and listen to the distant wind.

text: They don't ask twice. Hands are on your pack before you can react, shouting overlapping shouting, a shove that puts you on the ground hard enough to see stars. By the time they're gone, so is nearly everything you were carrying—the food, the medicine, the small comforts you'd allowed yourself to hope for. You're left sitting in the dirt with one bottle of water and the slowly dawning understanding of how much more dangerous this world just became.

A crash somewhere distant tears you out of sleep before you're ready for it, heart hammering before your mind even catches up. Every joint protests as you crawl upright, the cardboard nest doing little to disguise how hard the ground was. Grey morning light seeps into the alley, thin and unconvincing. What you can see of the street ahead is worse than you remembered—a tangle of burnt-out cars fused together by heat and time, blackened debris stacked chest-high in places. Sirens cry somewhere far off, for no one, answering nothing. Whatever fragile hope carried you through last night feels thin now, almost embarrassing in the daylight. The city rearranges itself while you sleep, you're starting to understand. It never holds still long enough to trust.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You grit your teeth and haul yourself over the wrecks. Your hands bleed, but you push forward.
You slip into the side alleys, every sense strained for danger.
You press into the shadows and watch, tension mounting as daylight slips away.

text: The wreckage groans under your weight like it resents being climbed. Broken glass finds every unguarded inch of skin, small cuts you'll feel later more than now. Halfway across, your foot finds nothing where solid metal should be, and the fall that follows sends a white line of pain up through your leg. You bite down on the sound that wants to come out—noise is a currency here, and you can't afford to spend it. By the time your boots hit solid ground on the other side, you're bleeding from three places you can count and breathing like you've run a mile.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You kneel and check the wound.
You grit your teeth and keep going, blood trickling into your boot.

text: The alleys twist without warning, one indistinguishable from the next, until they don't—until three figures step out to block the only way through. Gaunt, hollow-eyed, alert in the specific way of people who've learned that inattention gets you killed. Their gazes go straight to your pack the way starving men look at food. Fingers drift toward pipes, a broken bottle, something sharpened down to a point. Nobody's spoken yet. The silence does the threatening for them.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You approach with open hands, showing you mean no harm.
You slip into the shadows, moving with caution.

ifTrue.narrativeOutcome: You offer a rare battery as trade. The survivors give you a warning about the roads ahead.

ifFalse.narrativeOutcome: You search your pack for something rare, but find nothing worth trading. The survivors turn away, unimpressed.

text: YYou fold yourself into the shadows and let the minutes bleed past, one after another, indistinguishable. Hunger gnaws steadily at your insides, patient as a debt collector. Fear sharpens with every sound that might be footsteps and probably isn't. Stillness was supposed to be the safe choice. It doesn't feel that way anymore.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You close your eyes and let yourself drift, but sleep is dangerous here.
You force down a crust of bread, easing the ache in your gut.
You leave your hiding spot and press on.

text: You limp forward because forward is the only direction that means anything now. The road widens ahead, open and exposed, and your wound announces itself with every single step, a dull insistent throb keeping time with your heartbeat. Somewhere up ahead—maybe—there are voices. Or maybe the city's just talking to itself again, the way it does, wind through broken glass sounding almost like language if you're tired enough to believe it.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You press forward, determined not to let the pain stop you.
You shout into the emptiness. For a moment, there is only silence.

text: Something shifts in their posture—not welcome, nothing that generous, but a wary kind of permission. They step aside, opening a narrow path through the rubble just wide enough for one person to pass. One of them mutters something under his breath as you go, a warning about “shadows” further up the road, gone too fast to ask what he means. For one unguarded second, walking free between them, you remember what it used to feel like to trust a stranger. It doesn't last. But you remember it.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You offer a quiet word of thanks before slipping away.
You ask for more. They reveal a shortcut through the ruins.

text: A hand closes around your arm before you can react, grip tighter than it has any right to be on someone that thin. You wrench back, and that's when the pipe finds your chest, hard enough to steal the breath out of you. It's over in seconds—the kind of efficient, practiced violence that tells you this isn't their first time. Your pack is lighter when they finally let you go. Your hands won't stop shaking for a while after.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You struggle and manage to keep most of your supplies, but not unscathed.
You surrender your pack. Survival is more important than pride.

text: Sleep takes you further than it should have. You surface to a hand already inside your pack, fingers working quick and practiced through what little you have left, a shape crouched over you that resolves into a person only once your eyes fully adjust to the dark. However long you were out, it was long enough for someone to find you, and that thought alone is enough to flood you with adrenaline before you've even decided what to do about it.

choices.text: Scare them off with your flashlight or lighter.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You flash a beam of light and the thieves scatter.

choices.text: Let them take something and stay hidden.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You stay quiet as they take some supplies and disappear.

text: The worst of the city finally releases you. Ruined blocks give way, gradually, to blasted-out fields and the pale grey suggestion of mountains on the horizon. The air changes too—thinner, emptier, but somehow cleaner than anything you've breathed in days, like the ruins themselves had a smell you'd stopped noticing until it was gone. For the first time since you left the lab, you let yourself think the word Haven and actually mean it, actually let it feel possible rather than just a destination on a map. It's a dangerous thing to let yourself hope. You let yourself do it anyway.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You push forward, hope flickering in your chest.

text: Your hands search your pack with rising urgency, closing on nothing but empty wrappers and scraps too worthless to matter. The survivors watch you fail to produce anything, their expressions curdling from wary interest into something closer to contempt. One spits, deliberately, at your feet. Another just turns away, muttering something you're glad you can't quite hear. You back off with nothing to show for the encounter but a hot flush of shame and the unpleasant awareness of exactly how little you have left to bargain with, out here, where everything has a price.

choices.text: Retreat and look for another way.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You slip away from the survivors, avoiding their gaze.

text: The research district's perimeter looks like something tried to eat it and gave up halfway through. Barricades lie broken and rusted, swallowed by weeds that don't seem to care what the world used to be. Beyond them, HQ still stands—battered, but standing, the closest thing left to a stronghold in a city that stopped defending anything a long time ago. Somewhere inside is the Key. Three years of your calculations mean nothing without it. You've come too far to let a wall stop you now.

choices.text: Peer through a gap in the wall.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You spot two guards pacing the courtyard—and a narrow service door to your right.
A single guard glances your way. You duck behind debris just in time.

text: An iron gate blocks the way forward, its lock fused solid by years of rust and heat-warping. It wasn't built to keep people out, originally—more likely the opposite, something meant to protect whoever was still inside when things fell apart. Now it's just one more obstacle between you and what you came for.

choices.text: Force it open with your crowbar.
choices.narrativeOutcome: The gate screeches ajar—your ears ring as you brace for pursuit.
You find a half-buried service door under tangled vines, buying you a moment of silence.

text: A single guard holds the intersection ahead, weight braced against a spear that looks more improvised than issued—sharpened rebar, by the look of it, wrapped in cloth for a grip. He hasn't seen you yet, or he's pretending not to. Either way, you have seconds to decide how this goes.

choices.text: Offer him a ration to pass.
choices.narrativeOutcome: He smirks, pockets the food, and steps aside.

choices.text: Sneak past when his back is turned.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You brush past silently—and his boot nearly catches you as you slip by.

text: The corridor opens into what used to be a lobby, back when this building had people in it who came to work rather than people trying to survive the day. Shattered tiles crunch underfoot. Furniture lies overturned, exactly where it fell however many years ago. A reception desk sits buried under dust so thick it's become its own kind of architecture. Whatever's left of the shift schedule that used to run this place, you're about to find out if you beat it or not.

choices.text: Press on toward the office stairwell.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You slip through before shift change, heading for the stairs.

choices.text: Press on toward the office stairwell.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You arrive as the shift change erupts—uniformed guards swarm the lobby.

text: The staircase spirals up into darker floors above, and more than a few of its steps look like they'd rather not hold your weight—cracked concrete, some missing outright, all of it slick with a fine grey dust that makes every footing a small negotiation. Rushing feels tempting. Rushing also feels like exactly how people end up at the bottom of stairwells like this one.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You pick your way up without incident.
A rotten step snaps—your ankle twists as you tumble.

text: A heavy wooden door blocks the way, secured by both an old padlock and a keypad that's somehow still faintly lit—one of the last working circuits in a building that's mostly given up on electricity. Someone thought whatever's behind this door was worth protecting even after everything else stopped mattering. That's either a very good sign or a very bad one.

choices.text: Pick the padlock with your wire.
choices.narrativeOutcome: The lock clicks open—your heart pounds.

choices.text: Knock and bluff you’re authorized personnel.
choices.narrativeOutcome: Silence. You risk alerting any nearby guards.

text: A steel safe sits behind the ransacked desk, its digital lock somehow still holding after everything else in this building has failed. Whatever's inside, your old boss cared enough to protect it even as the world ended around him. You still remember the combination, or you think you do—three years is a long time to trust your own memory.

choices.text: Enter the combination from your old notes.

onSuccess.narrativeOutcome: The safe clicks open. Inside lies the Key—smaller than you remembered, stamped with the Scutum Project seal, and impossibly still exactly where it was supposed to be.

onFailure.narrativeOutcome: Three wrong guesses is enough. You give up on memory and go to force instead—the crowbar screams against steel, and by the time the door gives, your palm is bleeding and your patience is gone.

choices.text: Pry it open with your crowbar.
choices.narrativeOutcome: The door resists. Your crowbar splinters, and you slice your palm on sharp steel.

text: You cradle the Key in your palm like it might dissolve if you hold it wrong. Small. Sealed. Impossibly solid against everything else that's fallen apart today—the city, the plan, your own certainty about what any of this is actually for. Three years of work led here, to this specific object sitting cool and unremarkable in your hand. It doesn't look like it's worth dying for. You've come too far to decide it isn't.

choices.text: Tuck it safely into your pack.
choices.narrativeOutcome: The Key slides into your pouch beneath spare batteries, secure.

choices.text: Plug it into your portable reader to verify integrity.
choices.narrativeOutcome: The reader hums, then flashes "AUTHENTICATED." The Key's signature is intact—but precious time ticks by.

text: The Key is secured. Getting out is a different problem entirely—the halls between here and the exit are a maze you only half-remember from the way in, and somewhere in this building, guards are still doing their rounds, unaware yet of exactly how much has changed.

choices.narrativeOutcome: Familiar but risk repeated patrols.

choices.text: Strike out through an old elevator shaft.
choices.narrativeOutcome: The metal groans as you ascend. It saves time but draws unwanted creaks through the silence.

text: You hit the side exit at a dead run just as the roof gives a warning rumble and alarms finally catch up to what's already happened. Seconds later the doors behind you disintegrate in a shockwave of dust and debris, close enough to feel on the back of your neck. You don't look back to see how close. You just run, lungs burning, the Key a hard weight against your ribs, HQ's alarms fading behind you into the general noise of a city that's always screaming about something. Ahead: the highway, the open road, and somewhere past the horizon, if you let yourself believe it—Haven.

You collapse against the burnt husk of a car three blocks from HQ, chest heaving. Behind you, the alarms are already fading into the general static of the ruined city—no one followed. The Key sits cold and solid in your pocket. Your hands won't stop shaking.

choices.text: Stop. Breathe. Tend to what you can before you move again.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You force yourself still long enough to wrap what needs wrapping and drink what's left of your water. It costs you time you don't have, but your body thanks you for it.

choices.text: No time. Put distance between yourself and HQ first.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You're back on your feet before the shaking even stops. Adrenaline will only carry you so far—but for now, it's carrying you.

text: A few streets on, the road forks toward the overpass Caleb once marked on your map—if he meant what he said, and if you gave him reason to keep his word.

Caleb is exactly where he said he'd be, leaning against a rusted guardrail like he's been waiting for hours—maybe he has been. He straightens when he sees you, relief breaking across his face before he catches himself and hides it. “Figured you might actually make it,” he says. “Guess I'll stick around and see how far you get.”

The overpass is empty. Wind moves through torn plastic sheeting where Caleb said he'd be—but there's no one here, and no sign anyone ever was. Maybe he never meant it. Maybe he just never made it. Either way, the road ahead is yours alone.
Dawn breaks grey over the ruins. Ash settles like snow that never melts. Whatever's ahead, it starts with picking a direction.

Caleb falls into step beside you without a word for a while, boots crunching ash. Finally: “You didn't have to come back for anyone. Most people wouldn't have.” He says it like he's still deciding what to make of you.

choices.text: “I wasn't about to leave you standing there.”
choices.narrativeOutcome: Something in his shoulders eases, just slightly.

choices.text: “Don't read too much into it. I just needed the company.”
choices.narrativeOutcome: He huffs something that might be a laugh. “Fair enough.” But it lands a little colder than you meant it to.

text: The road splits three ways out of the ruins. Behind you, HQ's alarms have finally gone quiet—but that won't last.

choices.narrativeOutcome: Open ground, fast walking—but nowhere to hide if something's watching.
Slower going, but the embankments give you cover most of the way.
The longest route by far—but water means resources, if you're careful.

text: The highway stretches ahead, but the air feels wrong—skin prickling, old road signs scorched past reading. Somewhere close, background radiation is spiking, and the road splits around a collapsed overpass.

choices.text: Cut through the collapsed overpass supports—faster, but closer to the hot spot.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You move fast and low. Your dosimeter shrieks for a few seconds, then goes quiet again.

choices.text: Skirt wide along the guardrail—slower, but safer.
choices.narrativeOutcome: The long way round costs you time you don't love losing, but the reading barely twitches.

choices.text: Push straight through the middle of it.
choices.narrativeOutcome: Bad call. The reading spikes hard and stays there longer than you'd like.

text: You clear the worst of it, the dosimeter finally quieting. Ash-white residue clings to your boots. Whatever that place used to be, it isn't anymore.
The rail tunnel groans around you, dust sifting from the ceiling in a steady hiss. Something structural just shifted, somewhere ahead in the dark.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You sprint blind through the dark, boots skidding on loose gravel.

choices.text: Freeze and press against the wall.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You go still. Whatever's settling above you seems to settle back down.

text: A section of ceiling lets go behind you—close, loud, final. The way forward is clear, but the way back just isn't anymore.

choices.text: Keep moving. No going back now anyway.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You push on, trying not to think about how close that was.

text: The river's wider than it looked from the bank, current dragging hard at the debris caught along its edge. You'll need to get across one way or another.

ifTrue.narrativeOutcome: The rope earns its weight. You lash it to a fallen support and cross hand-over-hand, dry and steady.

ifFalse.narrativeOutcome: No rope, no choice. You go in and swim for it, current fighting you the whole way, colder and weaker on the far bank.

text: [END OF CURRENT STORY CONTENT] Day 5 is behind you, whichever way you crossed it. Day 6 hasn't been written yet.

Guilt follows you out of the pharmacy, brief and sharp, gone almost as fast as it came—there's no room left in you for anything but the next step, and the one after that. The sun climbs higher, harder, a physical weight pressing down through what's left of the atmosphere. Your legs go first, a strange watery weakness that has nothing to do with willpower. Then the world tilts. You reach for something to steady yourself and find only air. The last thing you register, before the dark takes you, is how quiet it's gotten—how the whole ruined city seems to be holding its breath along with you. Even careful men run out of margin, out here. Today, it seems, was yours.

choices.narrativeOutcome: Your journey ends here, claimed by the wasteland.

text: For one unguarded moment, relief gets the better of you—supplies in your pack, a little steadiness returning to your legs, the street ahead looking almost survivable. That's when the silence breaks. A shape detaches itself from behind a burned-out car, faster than a starving person has any right to move, and the impact takes you off your feet before your mind finishes processing what's happening. Pain arrives in flashes, disconnected: an elbow, the pavement, someone's breath too close to your ear. Whatever certainty you walked out of the lab with, it isn't here anymore.

choices.text: You're weak but you fight back!
choices.narrativeOutcome: You try to resist, but your injuries overwhelm you. Darkness swallows you as the world slips away.

choices.text: Fight back, pushing your battered body to its limits.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You muster your remaining strength, shoving the attacker aside and stumbling away into the shadows.

choices.text: Give up your supplies and retreat into the darkness.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You escape, but your pack is lighter and your heart heavier. The night awaits.

text: You hear angry voices at the pharmacy door before you've even caught your breath. Gripping what you managed to grab, you bolt for the back, vaulting a crumbling counter and crashing through a splintered window into the alley beyond. Shattered crates litter your path; your foot catches on twisted metal and you go down hard, pain exploding white through your leg. You force yourself back up, teeth gritted, and limp away with blood soaking through your pants, the pharmacy's angry voices fading slowly behind you. Later, hidden in a ruined stairwell, you bandage the wound with trembling hands and swallow a few of the antibiotics you risked everything for. The bleeding slows. The pain does not. Exhaustion settles over you like a second skin.

choices.text: Push onward, determined not to waste your hard-earned supplies.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You barely escape with your life, but at a cost.

text: The back door gives way under your shoulder and then you're running, lungs already burning, feet finding a rhythm your mind isn't consciously choosing. Shouts chase you through the alley maze, closer at some turns, farther at others—you can't tell anymore, and you're not about to stop and check. Your foot catches on a heaved slab of pavement and the ground comes up fast, scraping both palms raw. You're up again before the pain fully registers. Somewhere in the last two minutes you lost things—how much, you won't know until you stop, and stopping doesn't feel like an option yet. The city around you seems to grow colder with every step, dusk settling in like it's got nowhere else to be.

choices.text: Catch your breath and check your pack.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You hide in the shadows, shaking, and realize you've lost almost everything except one sandwich and little water.

choices.text: Keep running and don’t stop until you’re sure they’re gone.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You run and run, dropping only a single sandwich. By the time you stop, you're exhausted but safe for now.

text: The sun sinks lower, throwing long orange light across streets that haven't seen traffic in years. You walk with your head down, out of habit more than caution at this point—without what the pharmacy might have given you, every ache in your body feels sharper, every swallow drier than the last. The city seems to quiet around you as the light fails, shadows stretching thin and long across cracked sidewalks. Somewhere above, loose glass rattles in a window frame, stirred by a wind that carries the first real chill of evening. Near a rusted playground, something moves—a dog, ribs visible beneath patchy fur, nosing through a fallen trash can like it's forgotten what real food tastes like too. It hasn't noticed you. Your stomach twists at the sight of it, less from hunger than something closer to recognition. Everything out here is just trying to survive the day. Dusk is coming fast, and you still need somewhere to be when it arrives.

choices.text: Approach the dog and try to share food.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You crouch low and hold out a half of your sandwich. The dog sniffs your hand, tail wagging uncertainly. It takes the sandwich and runs. For a moment, you feel less alone.

choices.text: Search the playground for anything useful.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You search beneath broken benches and twisted slides. Your hands close on something useful in the dirt. A small knife.

choices.text: Move on and find a place to sleep before dark.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You keep walking, pushing past the ache in your belly, intent on finding shelter before night falls.

text: You push on because stopping isn't a real option anymore, lungs burning, ribs grinding against each other with every breath. The ground rises into a jagged ridge, the last real barrier between you and whatever comes next, and each step up it costs more than the last one did. You crest the top on willpower alone and your knees give out the instant the ground levels off. Blood has soaked all the way through your side, more of it than you want to look at directly. The medkit is right there, a few inches away in your pack, close enough to touch. Whether that's close enough to matter depends entirely on what's left in you.

choices.narrativeOutcome: You tear open the last medkit with shaking fingers, injecting the stabilizer and wrapping the wound tight. The world spins... then steadies. You lie back against the stone, breathing shallow, but alive.
Your hand fumbles at the medkit pouch... but you can’t even lift the flap. Darkness edges in. You collapse beside a weathered road sign half-buried in ash.

text: Your voice breaks on the shout, more desperation than sound by the end of it. For a long moment there's nothing back but wind moving through empty windows—and then, boots on gravel, unhurried, coming closer. A tall, wiry man steps out from behind a collapsed billboard, layers of scavenged clothing hanging loose off a frame that's clearly gone hungry more than once. He raises a hand slowly, palm out, more caution than threat. “I heard you,” he says, close enough now to really look at you. “You look like you've been through hell.” He offers a leather water pouch without being asked, nods toward a shaded patch under a rusted overpass. You drink like you've forgotten how water is supposed to taste—clean, cold, unbelievably generous. He watches you drink, and something in his expression shifts once you're steadier. His eyes drop to your pack. “I've got nothing left,” he says, quieter now, like the admission costs him something. “You got anything to spare?”

choices.narrativeOutcome: The man opens up. His name is Caleb, and he once worked logistics for a convoy for The Haven. He marks a safer route on your map and warns of raider traps ahead. “People like you… we need more of that,” he says.
You glance at your half-empty pack and shake your head. “Can’t risk it,” you say. The man gives a bitter laugh and stands.

text: The Scutum Project HQ stands ahead. Your objective: infiltrate the building, recover the Key, and escape before the government lock-down in 60 minutes. You can track elapsed time in your Inventory panel.

The gate gives way with a roar that echoes down the whole compound, announcing you to anyone listening. And someone is listening—boots hammering the ground behind you almost immediately, closing fast. Whatever quiet approach you'd hoped for just became a very loud problem.

choices.text: Stand and fight the first guard.
